items.subject: Grocery capture watchdog: 3 issue(s) 2026-09-20
evidence: ISSUE 1 (RUN RECORD, capture-run [ad] exit 1): grocery/out/logs/capture-run-ad-2026-09-20.log ends 'PS>TerminatingError(Invoke-Native): Cannot bind parameter because parameter Command is specified more than once' then 'commit/push threw: ...' then 'FAILED LANES: push'. The day's 27-file commit 8c64457ea was made and was NEVER PUSHED by that run. The line is grocery/capture-run.ps1:1108, 'Invoke-Native git -C $repo -c rebase.autoStash=true rebase -X theirs origin/main': PowerShell binds a parameter by any unambiguous PREFIX, so -C bound to Invoke-Native's own [string]$Command and -c then threw at BINDING time, before one line of the function ran.

ISSUE 2 (GRAPH SCHEMA moved): python graph/audit_schema_change.py before the fix printed 'THE SCHEMA MOVED AND NOTHING RECORDED IT. baseline 014da3370767862b -> live 0b94953fd784603d  added: table:sqlite_stat1'. sqlite_stat1 is created by ANALYZE, and graph/import/import_all.py:166 (backlog I212) runs one FULL ANALYZE at the end of the nightly import. graph/audit_schema_change.py's read_schema filtered only names starting 'sqlite_autoindex', so the estate's own nightly maintenance tripped its own schema alarm every day for a change no human authored.

ISSUE 3 (NO FRESH ROWS, Hy-Vee): grocery/out/regular/hyvee-regular-2026-09-20.json records ask_budget 15, asked 15, answered 0, refreshed_today 0, read_at_store_id 1466 (against 2026-09-19: asked 10, answered 9, refreshed_today 9). RE-MEASURED live at 13:20 against the Aisles Online endpoint at storeId 1466: 3 of 3 recently refreshed product ids answered (prices 1.25 / 8.29 / 6.49) and 11 of the 15 OLDEST product ids answered (6.99, 1.25, 0.99, 10.99, 2.99, 2.99, 1.99, 3.99, 3.99, 1.49, 4.99), 4 returned zero storeProducts. So the lane is NOT walled and those products are NOT delisted, and the 08:00 zero did not reproduce.

ALSO MEASURED for issue 3: of the 612 rows in that file with an as_of before 2026-08-01, only 24 resolve to a Hy-Vee product id through product-urls.json and 588 do not, so 588 rows can never be asked about at all. Get-HyVeeAskOrder (shipped 2026-09-19) puts exactly that bucket at the front of a 15-a-day queue.

surface_fix.what: quote every flag on the failing Invoke-Native call so it reads as data rather than as parameter names

items.root_cause: three independent defects, each of which makes an alert say less than it knows. (1) grocery/native-lib.ps1 declared [string]$Command and [object[]]$Arguments, and PowerShell binds a parameter by any unambiguous PREFIX, so ANY child flag that is a prefix of Command is taken by the binder before the function runs - 'git -C <dir>' is the commonest git form there is, and it killed capture-run's push stage. (2) graph/audit_schema_change.py's internal-object filter knew about sqlite_autoindex but not about the sqlite_stat tables that ANALYZE writes, so after backlog I212 added a nightly full ANALYZE the audit reported an unrecorded schema change every day for something no human authored - a real, correctly detected condition that needs nothing, which is alert fatigue by design rather than by volume. (3) grocery/pull-regular-hyvee.ps1's Get-HyVeeStoreProduct returned the same bare $null for a throw, a timeout, a response carrying only another store's offers and a genuine absence, so 'asked 15, answered 0' could not say which of the four it was - the fail-open-reads-as-empty shape, and UNCHECKED IS NEVER NOT-CARRIED is this estate's own rule about it.

root_fix.what: (1) remove the param() block from Invoke-Native and Invoke-NativeScript so every token arrives through $args and no child flag can ever bind, and refuse the removed named form out loud; (2) draw the schema audit's exclusion at 'who authored it' with a named predicate, excluding sqlite_stat* and deliberately NOT sqlite_sequence; (3) classify every Hy-Vee lookup through a pure Resolve-HyVeeLookupOutcome and count answered / other-store / empty / threw separately in the summary file and the coverage detail line
root_fix.exact_change: native-lib.ps1: both functions take $args, throw on an empty call and throw a named refusal on a leading -Command/-Path/-Arguments. audit_schema_change.py: _SQLITE_INTERNAL_PREFIXES = ('sqlite_autoindex','sqlite_stat') behind is_sqlite_internal(), used by read_schema. pull-regular-hyvee.ps1: Resolve-HyVeeLookupOutcome above the self-test gate, used by Get-HyVeeStoreProduct, feeding $script:HvAskThrew / HvAskEmpty / HvAskOtherStore into the summary fields ask_threw / ask_empty / ask_other_store and into the coverage detail line, plus a warning per could-not-look.

items.leaves_open: the Hy-Vee everyday lane still cannot re-read 588 of the 612 rows older than 2026-08-01, because they hold no product id, and the 2026-09-20 08:00 answered=0 itself is unexplained and did not reproduce - today's fix makes the NEXT occurrence name its cause, it does not price those rows

prevention.what: each fix is at the PRODUCER of the condition, not at the watchdog that reports it: the library whose parameter declaration stole the flag, the emitting check whose exclusion list was incomplete, and the puller whose single $null erased the difference between a could-not-look and an absence. No rule or exclusion data file is involved, which matters because this type has now returned twice.
prevention.exact_change: native-lib.ps1 declares no parameters at all, so the binder cannot take a child flag from any caller that will ever be written; audit_schema_change.py excludes SQLite's own ANALYZE output by a named predicate while keeping sqlite_sequence visible; pull-regular-hyvee.ps1 resolves four named outcomes and reports each count.

blast_radius.measured_by: no matching or pricing rule changed, so no product routes differently and no cell moves. The reach of the native-lib change was measured instead as its CALL SITES: grep over grocery/, ops/, lib/, meal-prep/ for Invoke-Native and Invoke-NativeScript found ZERO callers using the removed named -Command/-Arguments/-Path form and exactly ONE caller passing an unquoted dash flag (grocery/capture-run.ps1:1108, the failing line), which is fixed in the same change. The schema audit reads graph.db only. The Hy-Vee change adds counters and three summary fields and alters no price, size or basis.
blast_radius.risk: the native-lib change would break a caller written in the named form; there is none today, and one written tomorrow is refused with a message naming the positional form rather than silently mis-read. The schema exclusion could hide a real change named sqlite_stat*, which only ANALYZE creates; sqlite_sequence is deliberately left visible and has its own negative case.

items.subject: The knowledge store's nightly pass went RED
evidence: THE 2026-09-18 ROOT FIX DID SHIP AND IS WORKING. C:\Users\Owner\.claude\recall-sleep-log.jsonl (45,281 bytes, written 2026-09-20 04:39) carries each failing step's full output tail, and every finding below was read out of it rather than inferred from a keyword digest. That is exactly what the prior close set out to buy: 'a failure's explanation survives only if it happens to contain a keyword and is otherwise gone by morning'. It no longer is.

Today's pass: 4 of 30 steps failed - reflex fire rates (exit 1), forgetting (exit 1), memory clusters (exit 1), gate (exit 1). The gate's six FAIL lines, verbatim from the log: the lexical and semantic indexes disagree (2206 lexical chunks against 1988 embedded vectors, corpus moved since the last joint rebuild, remedy recall-reindex.py); reflex fire-rate caps; recall-forget unruled count moved off its mark; recall-consolidate unruled cluster count moved off its mark; automatic-recall.md section 2 does not name recall-brief-gate-hook.py; C--Codex-ThriftyCrew MEMORY.md links capture-watchdog-run-by-hand-pulls-family-fare.md, which git does not track.

The two reflex failures are numbers with their denominators: select-first-in-writing-pipeline fires on 228 of 5555 real commands (4.10%) against a declared cap of 3%, and concurrent-publish-shared-tree on 6 of 202 (2.97%) against a cap of 2%. Both need either a tightened pattern or a raised cap with a reason - a judgement, not a repair.
forgetting and memory clusters are reported by the pass itself as 'waiting on a judgement', not as breakage.

The Q3 floor question carried forward from 2026-09-18-35e0f5 is partly answered by today's numbers: the derive-floors step exited 0 and printed path holdout 5 of 106 fired 4.7% ok, alongside command 29 of 300, edit 41 of 300, prompt 14 of 124. The question of whether a floor derived at 04:38 on a store the same pass just re-derived is the verdict a re-run gives is STILL OPEN and is restated below.
